result:
The proposed answer 98 is too small. The correct minimum is at least 171.

**Reduction.** For a fixed prime $p$, let $S_p$ be the set of residues mod $p$ that appear among the $x_i$, and let $P_p$ be the partition of indices $\{1,\dots,n\}$ by residue mod $p$. Then $f(x_i)=g(x_i \bmod p)$ for some $g$, so the achievable value-vectors $v$ for $p$ are exactly those constant on the blocks of $P_p$, with the extra requirement that $v$ is nonconstant when $S_p=\mathbb{Z}_p$. Ana wins iff these sets are disjoint for every pair of distinct primes $p,q<100$.

**Constraint 1: at most one prime is incompletely covered.** Let $J$ be the join of $P_p$ and $P_q$. If $J$ has at least two blocks, take $v$ to be the indicator of one $J$-block. It is constant on blocks of both $P_p$ and $P_q$, and it is nonconstant, so it lies in both achievable sets. Ana loses. So $J$ must be a single block. In that case the only candidates are constant vectors, and a constant vector is achievable for $p$ only if $|S_p|<p$. Hence for every pair, at least one of $p,q$ must have $|S_p|=p$.

**Constraint 2: connectivity.** Think of a bipartite multigraph with vertices the residues used mod $p$ and mod $q$, and one edge per index $x_i$. The blocks of $J$ correspond to its connected components. Connectivity needs $n \ge |S_p|+|S_q|-1$. For a pair where both primes are fully covered, this gives $n \ge p+q-1$.

**Lower bound.** Only one prime can be incompletely covered. Whichever prime is excluded, the two largest fully covered primes are at least 83 and 89 (if 97 is excluded) or give a larger sum otherwise. So $n \ge 89+83-1 = 171$.

Since $98<171$, the claimed minimum is impossible. The argument that "98 consecutive integers" works also fails: the interval would cover all residues mod 97 and also mod 89, and the pair $(97,89)$ would need $n\ge 185$ to be connected. The answer is therefore not 98. My recollection is that the intended answer is 171, but I have not verified the matching upper-bound construction.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
